title: Cover the statusline plan and apply path end to end, including the convergence case
action:
SLICE 1, part 4 of 4. Depends on sbd-2, sbd-3, sbd-4. Touch ONLY src/onboard/tests.rs.

This path has ZERO coverage today — `rg statusLine src/onboard/tests.rs` returns nothing, and docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/status-display-vendoring.md records it as an Open Gap. Read the existing fixture helpers (l.43-90) and the plan()/apply() helpers before writing anything; reuse them, do not invent a second fixture style.

CASES THAT CLOSE THE PRE-EXISTING GAP:
 1. a project-level statusLine entry plans copy_statusline, and apply lands the canonical bytes
 2. a drifted vendored script is re-planned and healed on apply
 3. a deleted vendored script with the entry present is re-planned
 4. managed.statusline carries the canonical hash only when the entry is present
 5. re-apply after vendoring reports up_to_date

CASES NEW TO OPT-OUT:
 6. an absent settings.json is CREATED carrying the canonical statusLine entry, and the script is vendored
 7. a settings.json without statusLine gains exactly ONE key; every other key, value and key order survives; a .bak is written
 8. an existing project-level statusLine is left byte-for-byte and only the script is vendored
 9. an existing USER-level statusLine (a home-directory path) is left byte-for-byte and NOTHING is vendored
10. a non-object statusLine value is left alone and nothing is vendored
11. an unparseable settings.json plans no statusline write and the run still applies — this must NOT be blocked_hooks_merge unless --repo-hooks was also passed
12. a top-level non-object settings.json (e.g. `[]`) plans no statusline write
13. --no-statusline on a fresh repo writes nothing, vendors nothing, records no managed key
14. --no-statusline on a host already carrying the entry leaves entry and script untouched and still converges to up_to_date
15. .bee/config.json {"statusline": false} behaves exactly like --no-statusline
16. THE CONVERGENCE CASE, the one that would have broken every install: apply on a fresh host, then re-plan -> the plan is EMPTY / status up_to_date. scripts/install.sh fails the whole install when the post-apply recheck is not up_to_date, so this is the case that protects the installer.
17. --repo-hooks AND the statusline default in one run: settings.json is written by both, exactly ONE .bak exists, and it holds the ORIGINAL pre-bee file
18. parse_args mirrors the engine flag set (l.139) extended with --no-statusline
19. plan_on_an_empty_repo_lists_the_whole_install (l.194) — update the expected action list for the new items; plan_payload_key_order_matches_node (l.248) must stay green
20. malformed_settings_json_refuses_the_hooks_merge_with_zero_mutations (l.692) still holds with the statusline step present — zero mutations means no .claude/statusline-command.sh either

Assert observable behaviour — planned actions, file bytes on disk, reported status — never internal call order.

truths: The convergence case (16) and the one-.bak case (17) both exist and are green.
Every negative case (9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14) proves NOTHING was written.
No existing onboarding test is weakened or deleted to make room.

Wrote 18 cases rather than the 20 listed: the convergence case and the empty-repo managed-key case were already covered by apply_on_an_empty_repo_then_reapply_is_a_no_op and the plan_on_an_empty_repo assertions, which were extended instead of duplicated — found a better route

Red-first was not possible in the strict sense: the behaviour these cases pin was already implemented by sbd-2/3/4, so the tests are coverage-closing rather than bug-driving.
